description: Adaptation Clearinghouse is a web tool or resource listed in U.S. Climate Resilience Toolkit, a national climate-adaptation toolkit, published or maintained by Georgetown Climate Center. This site is an online database and networking site that serves policymakers and others who are working to help communities adapt to climate change. Coverage: the United States, or as stated on the tool page. The toolkit lists hazards: Air Quality, Changing Seasons, Drought, Erosion and Shoreline Recession, Extreme Cold, Extreme Heat, Flooding – Coastal, Flooding – General, Flooding – Rainfall-induced, High Winds, Landslides, Severe Winter Weather, Shifting Species, Habitats, and Ecosystems, Vector-Borne Disease, Water Quality, Wildfire. Assets: Agriculture and Food Supply, Aquatic and Marine Resources, Critical Facilities, Cultural and Community Services, Economy, Energy and Utilities, Forestry, Natural Areas and Wildlife, People, Property, Transportation and Mobility, Urban Landscape and Tree Canopy, Water Infrastructure – General. It is reached through the links recorded on this page, with the catalogue entry as the discovery route. Access is free of charge and open. The licence is not stated on the toolkit page (no licence or terms statement seen). Caveats: this record was written from the toolkit page, which was read; the tool itself was not opened or run, its licence and current availability were not checked, and the description may lag the source. It can support climate-adaptation planning and exposure screening. Related record: the catalogue-level record data-us-climate-resilience-toolkit-catalogue.
